content: 1. Always remove personal protective equipment (PPE) under the guidance and supervision of a trained observer, such as a colleague. 2. Ensure that infectious waste containers are available in the doffing area for the safe disposal of PPE. Separate containers should also be available for reusable items. 3. When removing the apron, lean forward and take care to avoid contaminating your hands. If the apron is disposable, tear it off at the neck and roll it down without touching the front area. Then untie the back and roll the apron forward for safe disposal. 4. Perform hand hygiene on gloved hands. 5. Remove the outer pair of gloves carefully and dispose of them safely. Use the appropriate technique as demonstrated in Step 17. 6. Perform hand hygiene on gloved hands again. 7. Remove head and neck coverings carefully to avoid contaminating your face. Start from the bottom of the hood at the back, rolling it from back to front and from inside to outside. Dispose of it safely. 8. Perform hand hygiene on gloved hands. 9. Remove the gown by first untying the knot, then pulling it from back to front while rolling it from inside to outside. Dispose of the gown safely. 10. Perform hand hygiene on gloved hands. 11. Remove rubber boots without touching them. If overshoes are worn, remove them instead. If the same boots are to be used outside the high-risk zone, keep them on but ensure they are cleaned and decontaminated appropriately before leaving the doffing area. 12. Remove gloves carefully using the appropriate technique and dispose of them safely. 13. Perform hand hygiene. 14. Remove the mask from behind the head. First, untie the bottom string above the head and let it hang in front. Then untie the top string from behind the head. Dispose of the mask safely. 15. Perform hand hygiene on gloved hands. 16. Use a 5% chlorine solution or an appropriate disinfectant for decontamination as needed.
